title: dev.sh check --json
description: The one schema every repo's `./dev.sh check --json` prints on stdout (PLAN-agent-groups.md §4.4): for each check the repo runs (its suite, audit, hooks, tree, ...), its status, counts, and failures with file:line and the role each belongs to. stdout holds this one document and nothing else; the exit code is 0 iff `ok`. The structure below is the JSON Schema; `x-rules` are the rules between fields that JSON Schema cannot say, each enforced by the `check-json` check under its id. tools/checks reads this file with a validator for exactly the keywords used here (checkslib/checkjson.py) and refuses any other keyword, so this file and the check cannot drift. That a failure's role exists in the repo's group (§4.4's second gate) is not checked here: it needs the roster, which tools/checks never reads.

ok.description: The verdict: false iff some check is `fail` or `error`. `unchecked` never makes it false, and never counts as a pass either.

checks.description: Every check the run covered, each reported (never only the first failure).

status.description: tools/checks' vocab.json statuses plus `error` (the check broke, or did not finish).

reason.description: Why it could not run; required when `unchecked`, optional otherwise.

counts.description: Non-negative integers. `failed` is required and equals the number of `failures`; others (passed, skipped, ...) are the repo's own.

failures.description: One entry per finding. Empty when `ok` or `unchecked`; at least one when `fail` or `error`.

file.description: Repo-relative path, or null when the finding has no file. Prefer null to a guess.

role.description: The role whose view this failure belongs to (PLAN-agent-groups.md §4.1 starts with code, tests, audit, docs): a failing test belongs to tests or code, a stale README table to docs.

x-rules.one-document: stdout is exactly one JSON document (whitespace aside): not empty, not text before or after it.
x-rules.exit-agrees: the exit code is 0 iff `ok` is true.
x-rules.verdict: `ok` is true iff no check's status is `fail` or `error`.
x-rules.counted: each check's `counts.failed` equals the length of its `failures`.
x-rules.status-failures: an `ok` or `unchecked` check has no failures; a `fail` or `error` check has at least one.
x-rules.line-needs-file: a failure with a `line` names its `file`.
